passage:
Every Sunday Swati wrote the whole month on a slate at the village dairy collection centre: which routes, which days, which cans. And every week it cracked. Rain washed out the lane to the far hamlet, the chilling machine stopped for a day, a helper fell ill.
By the third Sunday she was rubbing out more than she kept. "Why do you rewrite it every week?" asked Zeenat, who helped with the cans.
"Because it only holds till Tuesday," said Swati. She wiped the slate and this time wrote the coming week in detail, and across the remaining weeks just two rough goals: keep the far hamlet route, cut spoilage.
The next Sunday the slate barely needed a change.

qa.q: What did Swati write for the rest of the month?
qa.a: Swati wrote two rough goals: keep the far hamlet route, cut spoilage.

qa.q: What did Swati notice about her monthly plan that made her change it?
qa.a: Swati noticed she was rubbing out more than she kept and felt frustrated that the plan only holds till Tuesday.

qa.q: What else could Swati try if even the weekly plan started cracking?
qa.a: Swati could plan only the next two days in detail, since shorter plans are less likely to be broken by rain or machines.

qa.q: How might Zeenat see the new way of planning?
qa.a: Zeenat, who helps with the cans, may find the slate steadier and the week easier, since it no longer changes each day.

grounding: Noticing the plan cracks weekly, she plans only the coming week in detail and keeps the later weeks rough.

passage: Every Monday for a month, Ines had made a detailed plan for the whole month at the architecture firm in Lisbon: tasks by day, hours by task. Every Wednesday it cracked. A client changed a drawing, a site visit moved, and she spent Thursday redoing the entire plan. Her colleague Chidi watched her rewrite the chart for the fourth time. "You plan the month like you can see it," he said. Ines stopped. He was right. She could see about a week clearly; after that, it was fog. So she changed her method. Each Monday, a detailed plan for that week only. For the weeks after that, three rough goals on a sticky note. The next Wednesday a client changed a drawing again. She adjusted two lines and went back to work.

qa.q: How many times had Ines rewritten the chart when Chidi spoke?
What did Ines feel when she stopped at Chidi's comment?
qa.a: She felt a flash of recognition and some relief, seeing he was right and the problem was the method, not her effort.

qa.q: What makes the new method better?
qa.a: Detailed plans only for the week she can see clearly, with rough goals later, so changes cost two lines instead of a whole rewrite.

qa.q: How might Chidi see the change?
qa.a: Chidi is likely pleased his comment helped and glad to see Ines less stressed on Thursdays.

grounding: Noticing her plan cracks each week, she plans in detail only for the coming week and keeps rough goals for the rest of the month.

passage: In the hospital's quality office, Jyoti's month-long audit plan had fallen apart again by the second week. A ward postponed its inspection, a meeting was added, and her colour-coded chart was wrong. Akash, the data analyst who shared the office, found her re-drawing it on Friday evening. "That's the third time," he said. Jyoti put the pen down. "Because I keep planning what I can't know yet." She tore out a fresh page. At the top: "This week: detailed." She listed Monday to Friday, ward by ward, hour by hour. Below: "Rest of month: rough goals." Four lines. Finish ICU audit. Draft report. Two ward visits. Present to committee. The following Wednesday a ward cancelled. Jyoti moved one line.

qa.q: How many rough goals did Jyoti list for the rest of the month?
qa.a: Four lines: finish ICU audit, draft report, two ward visits, present to committee.

qa.q: How did Jyoti feel when she put the pen down?
qa.a: She seemed frustrated but suddenly clear, seeing she kept planning what she couldn't know yet.

qa.q: What else could Jyoti do to make the plan even steadier?
qa.a: Review the rough goals each Friday and turn only the next week into detail, as the plan now suggests.

qa.q: How does Akash see Jyoti's planning?
qa.a: Akash notices the repeated redrawing and seems gently concerned, prompting her to rethink.

grounding: Noticing her plan cracks each week, she plans in detail only for the coming week and keeps rough goals for the rest of the month.
